profile.name: Myel Lyel
profile.tagline: A traditional funeral dance of the Acholi people in Northern Uganda.
profile.insight: During funeral rites in Northern Uganda, men and women circle the burial site to express collective mourning through the movements of Myel Lyel.
profile.profile: Myel Lyel, also known as Myel Awal, is a traditional folk dance practiced by the Acholi people of Northern Uganda. It is performed during funeral rites as a communal expression of grief and mourning. Participants, including both men and women, move in a circular formation around the burial site. The practice is documented in the districts of Lamwo, Gulu, Pader, Kitgum, and Agago.
profile.profile_long: Myel Lyel, also known as Myel Awal, is a traditional folk dance originating from the Acholi people of Northern Uganda. The dance serves as a formal, communal expression of grief and mourning, specifically performed during funeral rites to honor the deceased. The practice is deeply rooted in the cultural life of the Acholi people, who reside in the districts of Lamwo, Gulu, Pader, Kitgum, and Agago. The dance has been common in the region over the past two decades. During the performance, men and women gather to move in a circular formation around the burial site. While the dance is a distinct cultural practice, it exists alongside other traditional dances of the Acholi people, such as the Larakaraka, Otole, Bwola, and Dingi dingi. Detailed technical aspects of the dance, including specific rhythmic patterns, footwork, musical accompaniment, and traditional attire, are not described in sources. As a funeral rite, the dance is inherently tied to the solemnity of burial ceremonies.
